summary.name: Codeflash
summary.one_liner: Codeflash is a performance-engineering service and AI agent that finds faster, cheaper versions of code (mainly Python and ML workloads), benchmarks them, and delivers verified changes as pull requests.
use_cases: catch performance regressions in new pull requests
summary.what_it_does: The codeflash-agent runs continuously across a codebase, looking for global and algorithmic optimizations. Each change is benchmarked against the original, checked against existing tests and auto-generated regression tests, and delivered as a reviewable PR with benchmark numbers attached. Senior performance engineers review and ship each optimization, according to the page. Continuous Optimization mode reviews new PRs to catch regressions as they are introduced, and it integrates with Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub. The page claims specialization in ML performance (GPU, CUDA kernels, vLLM, Hugging Face Diffusers, RF-DETR, SAM3) and lists example results such as a 90% infra cost cut and 13.7x faster token decoding merged upstream.
notable: Verifies every change against existing tests and auto-generated regression tests, with benchmark numbers in each PR
Runs in an isolated sandbox and states code is never used to train models
Offers SaaS, customer cloud, or on-prem deployment; SOC 2 Type 2 claimed
Cites merged upstream PRs in projects like PyTorch-style inference libraries (token decoding, WAN encoding)
caveats: Engagement-based service: starts with a 20-minute diagnostic call, so pricing is not published on the page
Marketing-heavy page; outcome figures are vendor-reported case results, not independently verified
Focus is Python and ML workloads; broader language support is not stated
